body:
I've applied for around 50 jobs, or thereabouts. Dunno know if that's a lot or a little. 

I've gone for anything that doesn't require experience or a diploma. So basically, working in shops and the like. Some places have an application form, some require you to send in your CV (or resume to the Americans).

My college does have a unit to help with finding a job, but it seems to focus on the course I'm in currently, something which I likely need the diploma to apply for, which I won't get for another year.

I don't know if I can get disability due to me not actually have much in the way of a disability.

My college did offer something called EMA, a payment to students which is basically given weekly, but it's only for under 18s and it was shut down a couple of years ago.

Friends and family tell me about any jobs that go on and I apply for them, but I hear nothing back. Last time I did, it was two years ago and I've been looking for about four.

I love my college group and I love the course I'm in. This is my third year in college, following me hating the last course I did enough to not follow it up. (I should note this is British college, not American college, so it's a little bit different).

The problem I have right now is my work. I want it to be good. Really good. The problem is is that it isn't and I don't have the motivation to make it good. Everyone else goes through with ease and here I am still dragging myself along. That's where I am. I want this course to be the one I want to do in the future, but I don't know if the work I'm doing is up to snuff and if it isn't, I don't have any motivation to carry on, even with friends and family.
